mainTopic: Giving צדקה when poor, the northern border at עכו, and whether a boat counts as ארץ ישראל
overview: The גמרא finishes a teaching from a פסוק in נחום: even a poor person who lives on צדקה should give צדקה, and then he will no longer be shown signs of poverty. It then turns to the משנה's statement of רבי יהודה that עכו is like the north of ארץ ישראל. A ברייתא seems to say ארץ ישראל reaches further north, up to כזיב. אביי answers that only a narrow strip of land runs north past עכו, and the גמרא shows from a פסוק in שופטים that a narrow road can serve as a landmark. Next, two ברייתות disagree about whether a גט brought on a boat counts as being brought in ארץ ישראל or in חוצה לארץ. רבי ירמיה says they follow a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the רבנן about soil carried on a boat. אביי says both follow רבי יהודה: a boat scraping the sea floor counts as ארץ ישראל, and a floating boat does not. רבי זירא applies the same מחלוקת to a pot with a hole resting on pegs. רבא starts to push back, and his reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even a poor person should give charity
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא learns from the word "וענתך" that even a poor person supported by צדקה must give צדקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And though I have afflicted you": מר זוטרא says that even a poor person who is supported by charity should give charity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues explaining the פסוק in נחום it was already discussing. מר זוטרא reads the word "וענתך" as being about a poor person (עני).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "וענתך" sounds like עני, a poor person. מר זוטרא learns from it that being poor does not exempt someone from giving צדקה. Even a person who lives on צדקה should give some himself.

keyTerms.meaning: I have afflicted you (a word linked to עָנִי, poor)
who is supported / who makes a living

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known rule that even a poor person should give צדקה.

phrases.english: "And though I have afflicted you" —
phrases.notes: נחום 1:12. The word sounds like עני, a poor person.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra says:
Even a poor person who is supported by charity
should give charity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the פסוק in נחום from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a poor person who lives on צדקה must give צדקה.

steps.title: The reward: no more signs of poverty
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains "לא אענך עוד": a person who gives צדקה will no longer be shown signs of poverty.
steps.simpleTranslation: "I will afflict you no more": רב יוסף teaches that he will no longer be shown signs of poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the end of the same פסוק. רב יוסף says it is a promise to the person who gives צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק said: give even if you are poor. This half gives the reward: ה׳ will stop showing that person signs of poverty. The two teachings together make a full lesson.
steps.whatToRemember: Even a poor person should give צדקה, and his reward is that he will not be shown signs of poverty again.

phrases.english: "I will afflict you no more" —
Rav Yosef teaches:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּב אֵין מַרְאִין לוֹ סִימָנֵי עֲנִיּוּת.
phrases.english: They will no longer show him signs of poverty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation of the same פסוק with the reward for giving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who gives צדקה even when poor will no longer be shown poverty.

steps.title: Is עכו really on the northern border?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה in the משנה and asks: does this mean עכו sits on the northern edge of ארץ ישראל?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי יהודה says, from רקם eastward, etc. Is this saying that עכו stands at the north of ארץ ישראל?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and points out what רבי יהודה's words imply about עכו. It is setting up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said that עכו is treated like the north of ארץ ישראל. That suggests the northern border runs right at עכו. The גמרא is surprised, because it knows a source that says something else.

keyTerms.meaning: a city on the northern coast
a place on the eastern/southern edge

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִרְקָם לַמִּזְרָח כּוּ׳:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: From Rekem eastward, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." stands for the rest of the משנה, which says עכו is like the north of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Akko
stands at the north of Eretz Yisrael?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּעַכּוֹ לִצְפוֹנָהּ דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָיְימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה's description of the borders of ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's statement in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies the northern border runs at עכו, which the גמרא is about to show is hard to accept.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the Land goes north of עכו
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that walking from עכו to כזיב, the west side of the road is ארץ ישראל all the way to כזיב, so the Land reaches north of עכו.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted it with a ברייתא: If someone was walking from עכו to כזיב, the land on his right (east of the road) is impure as 'land of the nations' and exempt from מעשר and שביעית, until you know it is obligated. The land on his left (west of the road) is pure, and obligated in מעשר and שביעית, until you know it is exempt. Until where? Until כזיב. רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי says in his father's name: until לבלבו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the משנה. It shows that land north of עכו, up to כזיב, still counts as ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking north from עכו to כזיב, the east side of the road counts as outside the Land: it carries the טומאה of ארץ העמים and has no מעשר or שביעית. The west side counts as ארץ ישראל, with all those obligations, all the way to כזיב (or לבלבו). So ארץ ישראל continues north of עכו, which seems to clash with the משנה that puts עכו at the border.

keyTerms.meaning: and they contrasted it (a contradiction from another source)
the land of the nations (outside ארץ ישראל, treated as impure)

steps.confusionAlert: Right is east and left is west here because the person is walking north, from עכו to כזיב.

phrases.english: And they contrasted it:
If one was walking from Akko to Keziv;
on his right — to the east of the road —
it is impure because of the land of the nations,
and exempt from tithes and from Shemitta,
until it becomes known to you that it is obligated.
On his left — to the west of the road —
it is pure with regard to the land of the nations,
and obligated in tithes and in Shemitta,
until it becomes known to you that it is exempt.
Until where? Until Keziv.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei says in the name of his father:
Until Lavlevu.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind the question in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that עכו is like the northern border
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats land north of עכו, up to כזיב, as ארץ ישראל, so the border cannot be at עכו.

steps.title: אביי: only a narrow strip goes north
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the main border is at עכו, and only a thin strip of ארץ ישראל runs north from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A strip goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי settles the contradiction. Both sources are right: the general border is at עכו, but a narrow strip extends north.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the main northern line, which runs at עכו. The ברייתא describes a thin strip of land next to the road that sticks out northward to כזיב. So the ברייתא is not moving the whole border, only adding this narrow strip.

phrases.english: Abaye said: A strip extends out.
phrases.notes: He means a thin band of ארץ ישראל runs north from עכו along the west side of the road.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the main border versus a narrow strip
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to move the whole northern border up to כזיב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The border is at עכו; only a thin strip continues north to כזיב.

steps.title: Would a תנא mark a border with a thin strip?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a תנא would really use such a narrow strip as a sign for the border.
steps.simpleTranslation: And would the תנא give a sign like this?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer. It seems odd that the ברייתא would use something as thin as a strip along a road as its landmark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Border signs are usually broad, clear areas. A strip only as wide as the land by a road seems too small to describe in this way. So the גמרא questions whether אביי's reading of the ברייתא makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: the teacher of a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: And would the Tanna give a sign like this?!

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's explanation that a narrow strip extends north
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems unlikely that a תנא would use something as narrow as a strip as a landmark.

steps.title: Yes: a verse also uses a road as a landmark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, and proves it from a פסוק in שופטים that locates שילה by a highway. רב פפא explains that the פסוק means east of the highway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. A פסוק also gives a sign this way, as it is written: "And they said: Behold, there is the festival of ה׳ in שילה from year to year, which is north of בית אל, on the sunrise side of the highway that goes up from בית אל to שכם, and south of לבונה." And רב פפא said: to the east of the highway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי. It shows that the פסוק itself uses a narrow road as a landmark, so a תנא can do the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places שילה "מזרחה השמש" of the highway. רב פפא explains this means east of the road, so a road is being used as a sign. If the פסוק can use something as narrow as a road, a תנא can use a narrow strip, and אביי's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: the place where the משכן stood

steps.whatToRemember: The northern border is at עכו, with a narrow strip of ארץ ישראל running north to כזיב; using a narrow road or strip as a landmark is normal, as the פסוק about שילה shows.

phrases.english: Yes;
a verse also gives a sign this way,
as it is written:
"And they said: Behold, there is the festival of ה׳ in Shiloh
from year to year,
which is north of Beit El,
on the sunrise side of the highway
that goes up from Beit El to Shechem,
and south of Levonah."
And Rav Pappa said:
To the east of the highway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and supports אביי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A narrow strip seemed too small to serve as a border sign.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק itself uses a narrow road as a sign, so a תנא may do the same.
steps.raayaObject: That a narrow feature like a road or strip can serve as a landmark
steps.raayaSupportSource: שופטים 21:19, as explained by רב פפא

steps.title: Two teachings disagree about a גט brought on a boat
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says that bringing a גט on a boat is like bringing it in ארץ ישראל. Another ברייתא says it is like bringing it in חוצה לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: someone who brings a גט on a boat is like someone bringing it in ארץ ישראל. Another ברייתא teaches: he is like someone bringing it outside the Land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It points out that two ברייתות give opposite rulings about a גט on a boat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our פרק makes a difference between bringing a גט inside ארץ ישראל and bringing it from חוצה לארץ. So the question is which side a boat falls on. One ברייתא puts the boat with ארץ ישראל and the other puts it with חוצה לארץ, and they cannot both be right as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in one ברייתא
And it was taught in another ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in one ברייתא:
One who brings a גט on a boat
phrases.notes: He means a גט that was written on a boat sailing in the waters of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: is like one who brings it in ארץ ישראל,
and it was taught in another ברייתא:
he is like one who brings it outside the Land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the discussion of the borders near עכו. It stays with the theme of what counts as ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about a גט brought on a boat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources give opposite rulings on the same case, so at least one of them needs explaining.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the two teachings follow two different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says there is no contradiction. One ברייתא follows רבי יהודה and the other follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is not difficult. This ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and that ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה settles the contradiction by saying each ברייתא follows a different תנא. In the next step he will show where these two opinions come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of saying the cases are different, רבי ירמיה says the תנאים themselves disagree. The ברייתא that says 'like ארץ ישראל' follows the רבנן. The ברייתא that says 'like חוצה לארץ' follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
This one ... that one; matching each source to a different opinion

phrases.english: רבי ירמיה said: It is not difficult;
this one is רבי יהודה, that one is the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the two sources to opposing תנאים (a מחלוקת).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought both ברייתות stated one agreed-upon rule, so they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect a real disagreement between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.

steps.title: The source: soil carried on a boat to ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says soil from חוצה לארץ brought by boat to ארץ ישראל is חייב in מעשר and שביעית. רבי יהודה limits this to a boat that scrapes the sea floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Soil from outside the Land that comes on a boat to the Land is obligated in מעשר and in שביעית. רבי יהודה said: When is this so? When the boat is scraping the sea floor. But if the boat is not scraping, it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show the מחלוקת that רבי ירמיה was talking about. The רבנן and רבי יהודה disagree about whether a boat counts as part of the Land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, a boat in the waters of ארץ ישראל already counts as the Land. That is why the ברייתא saying 'like ארץ ישראל' follows them. רבי יהודה counts it only if the boat touches the sea floor. That is why the ברייתא saying 'like חוצה לארץ' follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The tithe taken from produce of ארץ ישראל
The laws of the seventh year (שמיטה)
Scraping or touching the sea floor

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה argues about the soil itself. Both sides agree the soil came from חוצה לארץ. They argue only about whether the boat counts as ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
Soil from outside the Land
that comes on a boat to the Land
is obligated in מעשר and in שביעית.
phrases.notes: He means whatever grows in that soil while it is on the boat.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה said: When is this so?
When the boat is scraping the sea floor,
but when the boat is not scraping, it is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי ירמיה's claim in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה and the רבנן disagree about whether a boat counts as ארץ ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about soil from חוצה לארץ brought on a boat to the Land.

steps.title: אביי: both teachings follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אביי says both ברייתות can follow רבי יהודה. One speaks of a boat that scrapes the sea floor, and the other of a boat that does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Both this ברייתא and that ברייתא follow רבי יהודה, and it is not difficult. Here it speaks of when the boat is not scraping the sea floor. There it speaks of when the boat is scraping the sea floor.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer to the contradiction. He says there is no need for a מחלוקת, because the two ברייתות describe two different boats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה split the ברייתות between two opinions. אביי keeps them both with רבי יהודה and splits the cases instead. A boat scraping the floor counts as ארץ ישראל, and a boat floating above it counts as חוצה לארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both sources
Here ... there; each source is about a different case

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to settle the two ברייתות. רבי ירמיה says they follow a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the רבנן. אביי says both follow רבי יהודה: a boat touching the sea floor counts as ארץ ישראל, and a floating boat counts as חוצה לארץ.

phrases.english: אביי said:
this one and that one are both רבי יהודה,
and it is not difficult:
here, when the boat is not scraping the sea floor,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says the boat is like חוצה לארץ.

phrases.english: there, when the boat is scraping the sea floor.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says the boat is like ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction from step 8, instead of רבי ירמיה's answer in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases (scraping vs. not scraping), all within one opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the ברייתות must reflect a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבי יהודה. A boat touching the sea floor is like ארץ ישראל, and one that is not touching it is like חוצה לארץ.

steps.title: A pot with a hole on pegs depends on the boat dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says that whether an עציץ נקוב resting on pegs counts as connected to the ground is the same question as the boat dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: A pot with a hole in it that is resting on pegs is exactly the case argued over by רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא takes the boat argument from the last steps and applies it to a new case: a pot with a hole that sits on pegs above the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pot with a hole usually counts as connected to the ground, but here pegs keep it in the air, much like a boat floating above the sea floor. According to the רבנן it still counts as connected. According to רבי יהודה it counts only if it actually touches the ground, just as the boat must scrape the sea floor.

keyTerms.meaning: A flowerpot with a hole in the bottom, normally treated like soil connected to the ground
Pegs or stakes that hold the pot up off the ground
"We have arrived at the dispute": this case depends on an argument we already know

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the boat argument into a general question: does soil need actual contact with the ground, or is being close above it enough?

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira says:

phrases.aramaic: עָצִיץ נָקוּב הַמּוּנָּח עַל גַּבֵּי יְתֵדוֹת,
phrases.english: A perforated pot that is resting on pegs,
we have arrived at the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: This is the boat argument from step 10.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: עָצִיץ נָקוּב הַמּוּנָּח עַל גַּבֵּי יְתֵדוֹת, בָּאנוּ לְמַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the boat dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן from steps 10-11 and applies it to a new case, a pot on pegs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether an עציץ נקוב on pegs counts as connected to the ground depends on the dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן about soil on a boat.

steps.title: רבא questions the comparison: maybe רבי יהודה spoke only about a boat
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רבי זירא's comparison, suggesting that רבי יהודה's strict view may apply only to a boat. His full reason continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Maybe that is not so. רבי יהודה only said his view there, about a boat...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רבי זירא. He says we cannot assume the pot case depends on the boat argument, because רבי יהודה may have been talking only about a boat. This line is the start of his answer, and his explanation continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא treated the boat and the pot as the same kind of case. רבא suggests רבי יהודה's demand for actual contact may be limited to boats. If so, רבי יהודה might agree that a pot on pegs counts as connected, and the pot case would not be part of the argument at all.

keyTerms.meaning: "Perhaps it is not so": a standard way to reject a comparison
"He only said this...": limits a rabbi's view to the case he actually spoke about

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the רבנן and רבי יהודה agree about the boat. He only says that רבי יהודה's strict boat ruling might not carry over to the pot.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Perhaps that is not so –

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
